deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Updates for Dijkstra ledger rules, transaction building, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, guard scripts, and conformance testing
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples and cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Foundational runtime components including reactive workers, a chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal asks for ₳2,464,844 over 9 months, approximately $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.

The current proposal is a reduced resubmission from a prior ₳8.503M, 12-month proposal, with FTE reduced from 8.25 to 2.25 and the standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, and broad formal verification removed from scope.
Scalus components are reused in Cardano Client Lib, YaciDevKit, MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution.
Protocols and applications identified as built on Scalus include Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
The proposal says Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js has more than 20,000 downloads per month.

Dijkstra readiness is presented as necessary because Dijkstra introduces Plutus V4 support, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affecting smart contract development, evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and workflows.

Delivery is described as milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board, third-party assurance, public reporting, and open community sessions.
The proposal frames Scalus as shared Apache 2.0 open-source infrastructure intended to reduce repeated assembly work across many Cardano teams, tools, and products.
Lantr Engineering says every prior Scalus milestone was delivered on time and commits to on-time milestone delivery for this treasury-funded work.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus from July 2026 through March 2027, emphasizing reduced scope, maintenance of existing open-source infrastructure, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a first scoped application runtime with milestone-based governance.
